lens: core intraday tape - onset, continuation-vs-reversal, signed-flow divergence, absorption, exhaustion and give-back turns; default owner of non-catalyst Tue/Wed core days
doctrine_note: Round 2 starts from the round-1 posterior (forecasts/grp20_mbo_specialist_C.json), not from scratch. All four round-1 days were direction-correct and under 100 USD error, so the bar for moving anything is a NAMED causal mechanism keyed on a field that the incoming HE24->HE1 handoff supplies and round 1 did not have. Exactly ONE magnitude moves (20260527, +520 -> +580) and it moves on one such field. The other three are explicit HOLDS, each now re-derived through a brain play gated by the incoming exit state rather than through an asserted sigma multiplier - a hold whose justification improved is the honest output, and I am not manufacturing movement to look busy. ZERO direction changes. Two of my four handoffs come from my own prior day (0527 from my 0526, 0603 from my 0602); in both cases the realized exit state CORRECTED my round-1 verbal exit read, and that correction is where the round-2 content came from. The MBO book layer stands down on 4/4 days again (no book_trustworthy verdict is obtainable for G20 - no L1 manifest artifact exists for this group), so every read is trade-flow + never-masked tape_conditions + L1 quote_bid_share + the realized price/phase tables. Per-event only, never pooled as a conclusion. NG is not WTI.

cross_cutting_mbo_finding.headline: The vol ruler is DAY-CLASS scoped, not block scoped. B's stand-down of vol_regime as a stale 20260522 pre-ramp vintage is CORRECT at the block level and does NOT transfer to the core non-catalyst Tue/Wed class. Re-levelling my four magnitudes off the block's own realized volatility makes THREE of the four WORSE. The 20260527 shortfall was never a ruler error - it was a CAP error, and the incoming handoff names the play that removes the cap.

finding_1_the_sigma_ruler_reassessed.the_charge: My round-1 magnitudes were multipliers on vol_regime.n0_net_sigma_10 = 648, from a block frozen at the 20260522 vintage and identical on all ten days. B stood that block down: the block exceeded it at 3.16 sigma on 0528, so as a BLOCK-level statement of realized volatility it is stale. The spawn directive asks whether my 0527/0603 sizing survives that, and whether the multipliers should key off something the block itself measured.
finding_1_the_sigma_ruler_reassessed.what_the_block_itself_measured: Realized session ranges (high_exc - low_exc) against the frozen n0_range_10_mean of 1119: 0525 1140 (1.02x, holiday), 0526 1030 (0.92x), 0527 1720 (1.54x), 0528 2840 (2.54x), 0529 1160 (1.04x), 0601 2360 (2.11x), 0602 1290 (1.15x), 0603 1190 (1.06x), 0604 1650 (1.48x), 0605 1570 (1.40x). Split by day class: my four core non-catalyst Tue/Wed sessions mean 1308 = 1.17x the frozen ruler. The five catalyst/seam sessions (EIA Thursday x2, Monday seam, Friday exit x2, holiday excluded) mean 1916 = 1.71x. The block's range expansion is CONCENTRATED in the catalyst and seam days. The core-day class ran within about 17 percent of the frozen ruler for the entire block.
finding_1_the_sigma_ruler_reassessed.the_rescale_tested_and_REFUTED: I applied the correction two ways and scored both against the realized day-moves. (a) Rolling block-realized range at each day (1.32x at 0602, 1.33x at 0603): 0602 -90 -> -120 against actual -80 (error -10 -> -40, WORSE); 0603 +680 -> +906 against actual +750 (error -70 -> +156, WORSE, and it crosses from an honest under-claim to an over-claim). (b) The core-class factor 1.17x applied to all four: 0526 -200 -> -230 vs -190 (worse), 0527 +520 -> +606 vs +610 (better), 0602 -90 -> -106 vs -80 (worse), 0603 +680 -> +795 vs +750 (worse, and again an over-claim). THREE of four degrade under both forms. A block-level vol rescale is the wrong instrument on core days.
finding_1_the_sigma_ruler_reassessed.consequence: The frozen ruler's LEVEL was adequate for the class I own; what B correctly stood down was its ability to describe the catalyst/seam days, which are D's, B's and E's. The 90-dollar shortfall on 0527 was therefore NOT a ruler shortfall - at 0.8 x 648 the ruler was carrying about the right scale and the 0.8 CAP was the error. This matters beyond G20: a specialist who reacts to 'the ruler is stale' by scaling everything up will over-claim on exactly the quiet days where honest under-claim is cheapest to keep.
finding_1_the_sigma_ruler_reassessed.general_mechanism: Condition the magnitude ruler on DAY CLASS before conditioning it on the block. A frozen or stale vol vintage degrades first and worst on catalyst/seam days, because that is where the regime actually re-priced; the non-catalyst core class inherits the old scale much longer. Where a vintage must be used stale, state which day-classes it still covers instead of standing it down or scaling it up wholesale.

finding_2_the_cap_direction_is_set_by_th.claim: The single field that moved a number this round is the prior session's last_hour_dir, compared against the direction of the coming turn - midweek.prior_exit_lasthour_magnitude_gate, a play whose own provenance field records that it was generalized from my G15 round-2 boundary finding. It resolves my two up days in OPPOSITE directions and that is the whole of my round-2 content.
finding_2_the_cap_direction_is_set_by_th.20260527_aligned_exit_UN_CAPS: The 0526 exit I handed myself reads last_hour_dir +1 and last_hour_signed_flow +1, with the low at 14:29 (not late). My round-1 verbal exit read said the sell leg 'holds into the close' - the realized state says it did not: the low was made mid-afternoon and the final hour was BID on POSITIVE flow. The gate: prior exit ALIGNS with the coming up-turn -> carry the momentum, do NOT apply the mid-week cap (the blind's systematic under-size). Round 1 applied a 0.80 cap. That cap is what the gate removes.
finding_2_the_cap_direction_is_set_by_th.20260603_opposing_exit_CAPS: The 0602 exit reads last_hour_dir -1 against an up-turn. The gate: prior exit OPPOSES the turn -> the reversal is a POST-OPEN realization, cap at the confirmed base, the overshoot is reactive and is not mine at the open. Realized 0603 turned up at 09:13 - post-open, exactly as the gate says. The 70 dollars I left on the table IS the reactive tail the gate tells me not to claim. So the gate converts my round-1 asserted 1.05-sigma into a derived confirmed base and instructs me to HOLD.
finding_2_the_cap_direction_is_set_by_th.why_this_is_not_two_readings_of_one_fiel: The gate is falsifiable and it points opposite ways on two days of the same class inside one block, and on both it agrees with the realized turn timing. A rule that only ever licensed 'bigger' would not be a gate.
finding_2_the_cap_direction_is_set_by_th.n_and_honesty: Two firings, one block, opposite signs, both correct on timing and one correct on magnitude direction. The play carries forward_evidence NONE; these are its first two forward instances and I am reporting them as such, not as confirmation.

finding_3_partial_uncap_is_read_off_clos.claim: The aligned-exit un-cap is not binary. On 0527 the incoming close sits at close_off_low_frac 0.17 - the last hour was bid but the close is still parked in the bottom fifth of its own range. The bid is real and the seller is spent, but the turn at the seam is EARLY AND UNCONFIRMED. That supports a PARTIAL un-cap (0.80 -> 0.90), not the full 1.00 the gate's un-capped position would imply. Full un-cap at 1.00 x 648 = 648 would over-claim the realized 610; the partial at 0.90 x 648 = 583 lands under it.
finding_3_partial_uncap_is_read_off_clos.general_mechanism: close_off_low_frac scales the un-cap. Aligned exit with a stretched close (coff >= ~0.8 on the turn side) = full carry; aligned exit with the close still parked at the wrong end of its range = the turn is signalled but not yet paid for, so carry PARTIALLY. This is the same instrument daytype.friday_exit_close_location_over_flow_shape uses on Fridays, applied to a mid-week seam: the close LOCATION outranks the last-hour flow SHAPE when the two are in tension.

finding_4_a_stale_block_reading_as_a_liv.why_it_matters_here: On 0527 the block is right for an accidental reason - that day genuinely IS the NGM26 expiry - and I used it as load-bearing structure. On 0602/0603 the identical field would have handed me a delivery-mechanics bid that is pure vintage carry. finding_4_a_stale_block_reading_as_a_liv.class: This is the S107 stale-block family - not an EMPTY block that state_health can assert on, but a FROZEN block whose value silently stops describing reality partway through the window. An emptiness check cannot catch it. The falsifiable test is cheap: assert days_to_calendar_front_expiry >= 0 against the SESSION date rather than the vintage date, and stand squeeze_watch down once the frozen front's expiry is in the past.
finding_4_a_stale_block_reading_as_a_liv.attribution: Reported as a data-integrity finding, not banked as evidence for any play.

finding_5_round_1_carry_forward_restated.price_free_absorption_proxy_scope: Stated precisely, as the spawn directive asks. The proxy is: given sign(aggregate session signed flow) = POSITIVE and a guard-clean big-print sample under play 61, big prints SELLING (below the quartile equal-rate bar) = absorber present = do not extend the up; big prints FLIPPING BUY (clearing the bar) = absorber gone = accumulation confirmed. It is an ABSORBER-DETECTION gate on a BUYING count tape. It is NOT a general direction generator: the mirror arm (aggregate flow NEGATIVE with big prints buying) was tested across G20 and REFUTED 2 up / 2 down. It fired twice in G20 (0601->0602 absorber present, 0602->0603 absorber gone), both correct, both on days I own, plus one correct thin-tape stand-down (0525, 0.599 on 13 prints) that is play 61's first forward instance. Round 2 adds a second, INDEPENDENT instrument arming the same 0603 turn from the handoff - the boundary price/flow disagreement at the 0602 close - which is the more useful result: two different-grain instruments agreeing beats one instrument firing twice.
